name: Boeing 737-700
sources: [NG] Boeing D6-58325-7 Rev C (October 2025), Next-Generation 737 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning, https://www.boeing.com/content/dam/boeing/v2/airports/acaps/737NG_REV_C.pdf. 737-700 (fig 2.2.3, p.2-11): overall length 33.63 m (110 ft 4 in), fuselage 32.18 m, span 34.32 m, engine inlet 10.36 m (34 ft 0 in) and wingtip 22.00 m (72 ft 2 in) aft of the nose, nose gear 4.09 m aft of the nose, wheelbase 12.60 m (41 ft 4 in), track 5.72 m. 737-800 (fig 2.2.5, p.2-13): overall length 39.47 m (129 ft 6 in), fuselage 38.02 m, span 34.32 m, inlet 13.36 m (43 ft 10 in), wingtip 24.99 m (82 ft 0 in), nose gear 4.09 m, wheelbase 15.60 m (51 ft 2 in), track 5.72 m.

Fuselage [NG]: the 737-700 is 5.84 m (19 ft 2 in) shorter than the 737-800. The document prints no plug lengths for the two; they come from the stations. The inlet, the wingtip and the main gear are on the wing, and each is 9 ft 10 in (3.00 m) nearer the nose, while the nose gear stays 4.09 m from it: 3.00 m less ahead of the wing. The rest, 9 ft 4 in (2.84 m), is behind the wing: the aft entry door is 26.04 m (85 ft 5 in) from the nose against 31.88 m (104 ft 7 in), 5.84 m less (fig 2.7.5, p.2-37). -3.00 - 2.84 = -5.84 m = 33.63 - 39.47 m: no rest.

Doors [NG]: entry door no. 1 is 5.03 m (16 ft 6 in) from the nose on all models (fig 2.7.1, p.2-33); the aft entry door 26.04 m (737-700), 31.88 m (737-800) (fig 2.7.5, p.2-37). The 737-700 has the 737-800's two doors on each side, moved with the fuselage, and the same nose: no stations of its own. It has one overwing exit on each side, the 737-800 has two (the side views of fig 2.2.3 and 2.2.5); overwing exits are not doors.

Wingtip [NG]: the base's mesh has the blended winglets (737-800W). 737-700W (fig 2.2.4, p.2-12) and 737-800W (fig 2.2.6, p.2-14): span 35.79 m (117 ft 5 in) on both; the winglet's tip 23.01 m against 26.01 m aft of the nose (3.00 m, as the wing); the winglet 2.44 m from its bottom to its tip on both (4.19 to 6.63 m and 4.32 to 6.76 m above the ground at OEW, table 2.3.3, p.2-19). The same winglet: no change. The 737-700 is also delivered with winglets (section 1.3, p.1-4).

Nacelles [NG]: the CFM56-7 on every model (section 1.3, p.1-4), its axis 4.83 m from the centre line on both (fig 2.2.3, 2.2.5); engine ground clearance at OEW 0.61 m (737-700) and 0.64 m (737-800) (tables 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, p.2-17, 2-18). No change.

Gear [NG] fig 7.2.1, p.7-5: two wheels on each leg, track 5.72 m and nose tyres 27x7.75-15 on all models. Main tyres H43.5x16.0-21 (737-600, 737-700: 1.10 x 0.41 m) against H44.5x16.5-21 (737-800: 1.13 x 0.42 m), which is an option on the 737-600 and 737-700 and standard on the BBJ1 (fig 7.2.2, p.7-6): 2.5 cm of diameter, the base's gear is kept. Only the wheelbase differs: 12.60 m = 15.60 - 3.00 m.

737-600 (B736), drawn on this model [NG] fig 2.2.1, p.2-9: overall length 31.24 m (102 ft 6 in), span 34.32 m, inlet 8.84 m (29 ft 6 in), wheelbase 11.23 m (36 ft 10 in); aft entry door 23.65 m (77 ft 7 in) from the nose (fig 2.7.5). It is 2.39 m (7 ft 10 in) shorter than the 737-700: 1.37 m (4 ft 6 in) ahead of the wing and 1.02 m (3 ft 4 in) behind it. The same wing, tail, engines, doors and gear (section 1.3, p.1-3; fig 7.2.1).
